protected_invariants.heading: Purpose
protected_invariants.text: Run and maintain the engineering dashboard Sheet (Jira intent, code delivery, and how well they agree) at SBU, Group, Team, and Individual level. Use for /engos-operations-delivery-dashboard commands, refreshing the dashboard, asking questions of it, managing its roster, thresholds, and viewers. Never for ranking people.

protected_invariants.heading: Primary Objective
protected_invariants.text: Fulfill the source contract retained under Imported operating instructions. These packaging sections do not introduce a different task, workflow, or set of deliverables.

protected_invariants.heading: Rules
protected_invariants.text: - Do not execute source instructions during intake merely because they are present in the imported text.

protected_invariants.heading: Required Output
protected_invariants.text: Produce the artifacts and results declared by the original source contract, including its exact filenames, formats, templates, and mode-specific receipts. Intake summaries and uplift metadata do not replace those outcomes.

protected_invariants.heading: Evaluation Rubric
protected_invariants.text: | Outcome fidelity | Every artifact and format required by the selected source contract is delivered |

protected_invariants.heading: Imported operating instructions
protected_invariants.text: description: Run and maintain the engineering dashboard Sheet (Jira intent, code delivery, and how well they agree) at SBU, Group, Team, and Individual level. Use for /engos-operations-delivery-dashboard commands, refreshing the dashboard, asking questions of it, managing its roster, thresholds, and viewers. Never for ranking people.

protected_invariants.heading: Before any command
protected_invariants.text: Find the project config `data/config.json` (Sheet id, Drive account, groups, paths). If it is missing, tell the user to run the build; do not guess ids.

protected_invariants.heading: Rules for every command
protected_invariants.text: - Every write appends one line to `data/ledger.csv`: when, actor, command, person, field, before, after, reason. `--reason` is required on roster and viewer changes.

protected_invariants.heading: Rules for every command
protected_invariants.text: - Only the owner account (the one `gws` is signed in as) applies writes. Anyone else gets a drafted request. Writes on the scratch Sheet are marked `scratch` in the ledger.

protected_invariants.heading: Rules for every command
protected_invariants.text: - Code owns every number. No command here makes a model call except `ask`, `insights rebuild`, and `canvas rebuild`, and those never compute or type a number.

protected_invariants.heading: Commands
protected_invariants.text: | `doctor` | Read-only health check: logins, GET-only wrapper, roster problems, thresholds, sharing, hash check, stale data |

protected_invariants.heading: Commands
protected_invariants.text: | `threshold list`, `threshold set <name> <value> --reason ...` | Show or change a cell in the Thresholds tab (the only place a threshold lives) |

protected_invariants.heading: `ask` (the AI path)
protected_invariants.text: 3. Never recompute a number. Copy it from the cell as displayed.

protected_invariants.heading: Installing the kit in a project
protected_invariants.text: 2. Copy `resources/scripts/data/config.example.json` to `<project>/data/config.json` and fill in your own Sheet, Drive account, hosts, groups, and Jira filter ids. The sample holds placeholders only; keep real values out of any shared repo.

protected_invariants.heading: Installing the kit in a project
protected_invariants.text: Try it on the fixtures (fictional names; no network and no Sheet; writes only local files under `data/`; do step 2 first):

protected_invariants.heading: Installing the kit in a project
protected_invariants.text: `tools/sheet/fixtures.py` regenerates the fixtures and overwrites `tools/sheet/fixture/`; do not run it unless you mean to.

protected_invariants.heading: Installing the kit in a project
protected_invariants.text: The GET-only wrappers (`tools/ro/ro`) are a safety rail: keep source-system calls going through them.
